card.title: Director of Plant Operations
card.description:
**Essential Functions and Responsibilities:**

* Maintain a clean and organized work environment.
* Assure compliance of life safety regulations, based on state specific requirements. This includes staff training, documentation and complete record keeping.
* Routinely inspect the physical plant and provide routine preventative maintenance within recommended routines. Inspections should be documented completion, repairs logged and completed. All repairs should coincide with Fields Senior Living standards.
* Routinely coordinate, direct and document required fire drills and training. Including annual full inspections and inservice with employees.
* Establish and maintain schedule of service of equipment and systems.
* On a routine basis, inspection of resident’s apartments. Ensuring cleanliness and documenting needed repairs. Repairs should be done in a timely manner and communication to nursing team on any unsafe living conditions.
* Maintain outside yard care, whether performed by facility staff or contract service
* Maintain facility to meet all regulatory requirements.
* Turn apartments when move outs occur within 72 hours of move outs. Ensure walk through of apartment is done prior to move out.
* Ordering of all plant operations supplies and products, maintaining budget.
* Oversight of housekeeping services. Leading the housekeeping supervisor and team to success. Ensuring apartments and common areas are cleaned to Fields Senior Living standards.
* Complete work orders within 48 hours of submission. Documented and followed up with resident, staff or family.
* All other duties as assigned.

 

**Additional Functions:**

* Must possess qualities of leadership, tact, and adaptability to change. Must be neat in appearance, pleasant personality, be congenial to fellow team members, residents, families, and the public in general. Must be capable of using own judgement and initiative in daily duties.
* Must have strong organizational skills, as well as the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines.
* Must be detail and team-work oriented.
* Must attend required in-services/ workshops to further education of skills and community requirements.

 

**Qualifications:**

* Must be Drug free and submit to Urinary Analysis Drug screening upon hire and routinely.
* Must be able to pass Criminal Background Check, Health Screening including TB test.
* Must be eighteen (18) years old.
* Have working knowledge of electrical systems, air conditioning systems, heating systems, intercom systems, fire detention systems, plumbing, water and sewage systems, and maintenance of generator.
* Must have good mechanical aptitude and be able to perform general maintenance in electrical, plumbing and carpentry areas.
* Maintain current CPR and First Aid Certification.
* A passion for helping seniors, especially those living with Dementia and Alzheimer’s Disease.
* Experience working with Dementia residents.
* Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, verbally and in writing in standard English.
* Able to work all shifts to ensure staffing coverage when needed.
* **The employee shall be responsible for maintaining the integrity of Fields Senior Living.**

**Physical Demands and Requirements:**

* Maintain ability to lift 50 pounds; to stand or walk throughout the vast majority of the workday; and to frequently push, pull, bend, twist and reach.
* Must be willing to be active and on feet during entire work shift.
* Involves light to heavy physical activity performing non-strenuous and strenuous activities.
* Must have sufficient manual dexterity to work with the fingers and to reach/hand items

card.title: Plant Manager - Ready Mix Concrete - Solsberry IN
card.description:
About the Opportunity:

Are you a proven leader who thrives on building strong teams and delivering exceptional service? At SRM Concrete, our Plant Managers are the driving force behind our commitment to operational excellence and customer satisfaction. As a Plant Manager, you’ll lead by example—empowering your team, optimizing daily operations, and ensuring every load meets the highest standards of safety, quality, and service.

If you’re passionate about leadership, logistics, and making a positive impact in your community, this is your opportunity to join a company that values integrity, teamwork, and growth.

Your Mission & Key Responsibilities:

* Lead with purpose: Inspire, coach, and develop your plant team to achieve operational excellence and deliver outstanding service to every customer.
* Oversee daily plant operations: Manage staff scheduling, load planning, and route optimization to ensure efficient and timely concrete deliveries.
* Champion customer service: Collaborate with drivers, dispatch, and sales teams to exceed customer expectations and resolve any issues with urgency and care.
* Drive performance: Implement and monitor key metrics to assess plant efficiency, productivity, and service quality.
* Foster a culture of safety: Ensure full compliance with safety regulations and company policies, creating a safe and positive work environment for all.
* Promote teamwork: Conduct regular meetings to review performance, address challenges, and celebrate successes.
* Build relationships: Develop strong connections with customers, suppliers, and SRM team members to support seamless operations.
* Contribute to growth: Participate in strategic planning and budgeting, sharing insights to enhance plant efficiency and profitability.

What Sets You Apart:

* Inspirational leadership style with a passion for developing high-performing teams.
* Commitment to delivering exceptional customer service and building lasting relationships.
* Strong organizational and problem-solving skills; able to prioritize and adapt in a fast-paced environment.
* Deep understanding of logistics, supply chain management, or plant operations—experience in the concrete or construction industry is highly valued.
* Proficiency with dispatch software, Microsoft Office Suite, and a willingness to learn new systems.
* Knowledge of DOT regulations and safety standards for transportation and delivery.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; you build trust with team members, customers, and partners.
* Dedication to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Willingness to undergo SRM’s pre-employment screenings.

About SRM:

SRM Concrete (Smyrna Ready Mix) is a family-owned, values-driven leader in the ready mix concrete industry. Founded in 1999 with a single plant in Smyrna, Tennessee, we’ve grown to over 600 locations nationwide by focusing on quality, integrity, and service. Our mission is to serve our customers, our communities, and our team members with excellence—every load, every day.Why Join SRM Concrete?

**Why Join SRM Concrete?**

* **Growth & Advancement:** Be part of a rapidly expanding company with real opportunities to grow your career.
* **Impact:** Lead a team that plays a pivotal role in building America’s future.
* **Competitive Pay & Exceptional Benefits:** Low-cost medical, dental, vision, STD, LTD, and life insurance; paid holidays; PTO/vacation; 401k with $100 weekly match; family days; and more!
* **Team Culture:** We value hard work, respect, and teamwork. We support each other, recognize a job well done, and believe in doing what’s right—on the job and in the community. You’ll find a straightforward, dependable environment where every team member matters.

At SRM Concrete, you’re more than a manager—you’re a valued team member helping to build America’s future. If you’re ready to say “YES” to new opportunities and deliver service that sets the standard in our industry, apply today and join the SRM family!

card.description:
**When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.**

The Director of Plant Operations is responsible for the leadership and oversight of all facilities-related functions at Lahey Clinic, including the Burlington campus, Lahey Clinic North in Peabody, and multiple offsite buildings. This role manages a multidisciplinary team that includes skilled trades, the Grounds team, and the Safety Department. The Director ensures the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of all building systems and infrastructure, and maintains full compliance with all regulatory and accreditation requirements. This position plays a critical role in supporting the hospital’s mission by ensuring a safe, functional, and responsive environment of care through effective facilities management, infrastructure planning, and team leadership.

**Job Description:**

1. Provide leadership and direction for all skilled trades, including electrical, HVAC, plumbing, carpentry, painting, locksmithing, general maintenance, and grounds operations.

2. Ensure full compliance with all applicable regulations and standards, including Joint Commission, DPH, CMS, OSHA, and NFPA.

3. Oversee facilities operations at Lahey Clinic North and all offsite buildings, ensuring alignment with main campus standards.

4. Lead the development and execution of preventive maintenance programs, capital renewal strategies, and infrastructure planning.

5. Collaborate with hospital leadership, Design & Construction, and Environmental Health & Safety on projects, renovations, and upgrades.

6. Develop and manage annual operating and capital budgets; monitor expenditures and lead cost-effective resource use.

7. Cultivate a high-performing, service-oriented team culture focused on reliability, safety, and continuous improvement.

8. Serve as a key leader in regulatory readiness and response efforts related to physical environment, life safety, and utility systems.

9. Incorporates Lahey Clinic Mission Statement and Goals into daily activities.

10. Complies with all Lahey Health Policies.

11. Complies with behavioral expectations of the department and Lahey Health.

12. Maintains courteous and effective interactions with colleagues and patients.

13. Demonstrates an understanding of the job description, performance expectations, and competency assessment.

14. Demonstrates a commitment toward meeting and exceeding the needs of our customers and consistently adheres to Customer Service standards.

15. Participates in departmental and/or interdepartmental quality improvement activities.

16. Participates in and successfully completes Mandatory Education.

17. Performs all other duties as needed or directed to meet the needs of the department.

**Minimum Qualifications** :

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, or related field. Relevant experience may be substituted for the educational requirement.

Licensure, Certification, Registration:

* Certified Healthcare Facility Manager (CHFM) required within 1 year of hire, or when eligible.

Skills, Knowledge & Abilities:

* Strong knowledge of building systems, life safety, and healthcare regulatory requirements

* Ability to lead teams across multiple sites and manage a 24/7 operation

card.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
card.description:
**Company Description**

Domino’s Pizza, which began in 1960 as a single store location in Ypsilanti, MI, has had a lot to celebrate lately: we’re a reshaped, reenergized brand of honesty, transparency and accountability – not to mention, great food! In the rise to becoming a true technology leader, the brand is now consistently one of the top five companies in online transactions and 65% of our sales in the U.S. are taken through digital channels. The brand continues to ‘deliver the dream’ to local business owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores. That’s just the tip of the iceberg…or as we might say, one “slice” of the pie! If this sounds like a brand you’d like to be a part of, consider joining our team!

 **Job Description**

The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.

Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.

**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**

In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:

Be Curious

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

 
**Additional Information**

Benefits: 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

card.title: Professor of Practice & Manufacturing Extension Program Director
card.description:
**Department:**

The Center for Manufacturing Excellence's (CME)

**Job Summary:**

Performs duties in instruction, including the teaching of practical skills and demonstrating best professional practices. Not eligible for tenure.

**Job Description:**

The Professor of Practice & Manufacturing Extension Program Director provides leadership for the Center for Manufacturing Excellence's (CME) manufacturing extension and industry engagement activities. The position connects University expertise, educational resources, faculty, and students with manufacturers throughout Mississippi and the region to strengthen organizational performance, workforce capability, operational excellence, and competitiveness. As a Professor of Practice, the individual also contributes to CME's academic mission through teaching, applied scholarship, student engagement, and curriculum development. The position is practice oriented and is not expected to conduct traditional academic research. The rank of the Professor of Practice appointment will be determined based on the selected candidate’s qualifications and relevant professional experience.

 

The Manufacturing Extension Program Director role will develop, lead, and grow a comprehensive manufacturing extension program responsive to the needs of manufacturers and other industry partners. Working collaboratively with CME faculty and staff, industry, and economic and workforce development partners, the incumbent identifies industry needs and develops training, technical assistance, professional education, applied projects, and other services to address those needs.

 

The position will emphasize industry engagement, operational excellence and continuous improvement, applied problem solving, external funding, professional and graduate education, and measurable extension impact. The Program Director will also teach graduate and undergraduate courses consistent with the individual's expertise and support CME's Graduate Certificate in Operational Leadership and related academic and professional programs.

 

*Join the Ole Miss Family — Build Your Legacy Here!*

**Job Responsibilities:**

**Examples of Work Performed**

 

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for CME's manufacturing extension program and develop a sustainable structure and portfolio of industry-facing services.
* Build and maintain relationships with manufacturers, industry associations, economic development organizations, workforce development agencies, and other external partners.
* Identify manufacturing needs and develop customized or scalable training, technical assistance, and applied problem-solving initiatives.
* Develop and deliver programs in areas such as Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, continuous improvement, operational excellence, project management, manufacturing leadership, supply chain, and operations strategy, consistent with the individual's expertise.
* Coordinate CME faculty, staff, students, University resources, and external subject-matter experts in support of industry projects and extension activities.
* Teach CME graduate and undergraduate courses and contribute to curriculum development to include online coursework and course/program assessment.
* Mentor and engage students in industry sponsored projects, applied scholarship, internships, and other experiential learning activities.
* Produce and disseminate practice oriented applied scholarship, including industry case studies, technical reports, professional presentations, instructional materials, and best practice resources.
* Identify and pursue grants, contracts, sponsorships, fee-based programming, and other external funding to support and expand manufacturing extension activities.
* Establish measures of program effectiveness and communicate extension outcomes and impact to industry partners, University leadership, funding organizations, and other stakeholders.
* Represent CME and the University at manufacturing conferences, industry meetings, professional organizations, and economic development activities.
* Identify emerging manufacturing trends, technologies, workforce challenges, and practices and translate them into new CME programs, services, and educational opportunities.

**Education Qualifications:**

Terminal Degree (Required)

**Experience:**

Project Management

**Interview Requirement:**

Interview Requirements: Any candidate who is called for an interview must notify the Department of Equal Opportunity/Regulatory Compliance in writing of any reasonable accommodation needed prior to the date of the interview.

**EEO Statement:**

The University of Mississippi provides equal opportunity in any employment practice, education program, or education activity to all qualified persons. The University complies with all applicable laws regarding equal opportunity and affirmative action and does not unlawfully discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment based upon race, color, gender, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, citizenship, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or genetic information.

**Background Check Statement:**

The University of Mississippi is committed to providing a safe campus community. UM conducts background investigations for applicants being considered for employment. Background investigations include a criminal history record check, and when appropriate, a financial (credit) report or driving history check.

card.description:
**Job Description:**
====================

NOTE: This role is based in New York City and encourages a minimum of two days per week in the SoHo office. Some roles or teams may require additional in-office attendance if the essential functions of the role require it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Senior Director, Merchandise Manufacturing & Strategic Sourcing is a key global leadership role responsible for the strategic sourcing, manufacturing, commercialization, and production execution of Scholastic's merchandise portfolio supporting Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade Publishing, Discovery Fairs, and future consumer product initiatives.

Reporting directly to the SVP Manufacturing who is responsible for Global Supply Chain and Procurement, this position serves as the critical bridge between Product Development, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Publishing, and global manufacturing partners.

This leader partners with internal stakeholders from the earliest stages of product ideation, providing expertise in product engineering, sourcing strategy, manufacturing capabilities, material selection, cost optimization, and production feasibility. The objective is to transform creative concepts into high-quality, innovative products that deliver exceptional customer experiences while achieving aggressive cost, quality, and speed-to-market objectives.

The role oversees a global sourcing portfolio exceeding $200 million annually and leads an international team of approximately 12 professionals located across the United States and India. The position may be based in the United States, China, or India and requires extensive collaboration with domestic and international suppliers and manufacturing partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

**Product Development, Ideation & Publishing Partnership**

* Serve as a strategic partner to Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Book Fairs, Book Clubs, Trade, and other stakeholders to translate creative concepts and intellectual property into compelling, manufacturable products.
* Engage early in product ideation, bringing manufacturing and sourcing expertise to decisions around materials, formats, construction, packaging, features, price points, and production methods.
* Proactively introduce new product concepts, materials, manufacturing capabilities, and supplier innovations that expand Scholastic's product opportunities.
* Partner throughout the development cycle from concept, specification, prototyping, sampling, and costing through pproval and production.
* Challenge and improve concepts where appropriate to enhance consumer appeal, quality, manufacturability, sustainability, speed, and cost.

**Consumer Products & Sourcing Strategy**

* Lead development of the sourcing and manufacturing strategy supporting Scholastic's expanding consumer-products and merchandise initiatives.
* Partner with business and publishing leadership to identify new product categories and opportunities across Book Fairs, Discovery Fairs, retail, e-commerce, licensing, and other emerging channels.
* Develop category sourcing strategies addressing manufacturing regions, supplier capabilities, cost, lead times, minimum quantities, tooling, quality, and supply-chain risk.
* Build a proactive pipeline of product ideas and manufacturing capabilities that can be regularly presented to internal stakeholders.
* Maintain awareness of consumer trends, emerging categories, materials, and manufacturing technologies and translate those insights into actionable product opportunities.

**Global Vendor Development & Innovation**

* Proactively identify and develop innovative manufacturers and product-development partners, particularly those offering engineering expertise, rapid prototyping, unique materials, creative capabilities, and new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop suppliers that can function as extensions of Scholastic's product-development organization, proactively bringing forward new concepts and capabilities.
* Continuously evaluate the supplier portfolio to improve competitiveness, increase speed, diversify supply, reduce risk, and enable entry into new categories.

**Global Sourcing, Cost & Operational Leadership**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive global sourcing strategy supporting more than $200 million in annual product expense.
* Establish sourcing roadmaps and supplier-diversification strategies that anticipate future business requirements and reduce dependency on individual suppliers or regions.
* Ensure products consistently meet expectations for quality, safety, regulatory compliance, sustainability, cost, and on-time delivery.

**Supplier Engagement & Global Travel**

* Maintain direct senior-level engagement with strategic manufacturing partners and regularly visit supplier facilities to evaluate capabilities, innovation, quality, capacity, and operational performance.
* Significant international travel is expected, with consistent travel to Asia, particularly China and India, as well as other global sourcing markets as required.
* Use supplier visits as product-development and innovation opportunities to identify new materials, manufacturing processes, capabilities, and product concepts for Scholastic.
* Participate in relevant trade shows, sourcing events, and supplier innovation sessions to identify emerging capabilities and potential partners.

**Organizational Leadership**

* Lead and develop a global organization of approximately 12 professionals across the United States and India.
* Build a culture combining sourcing discipline with creativity, product knowledge, commercial thinking, and an entrepreneurial approach to product development.
* Develop team capabilities in product ideation, product development, supplier innovation, value engineering, and strategic sourcing.
* Build strong partnerships across Publishing, Editorial, Design, Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, and senior leadership, positioning the organization as a strategic product-development partner.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success will be measured through product development and innovation, cost per unit and total landed-cost, speed to market, supplier innovation and diversification, quality and compliance, on-time performance.

**About Scholastic**

For more than 100 years, Scholastic Corporation (NASDAQ: SCHL) has been meeting children where they are – at school, at home and in their communities – by creating quality content and experiences, all beginning with literacy. Scholastic delivers stories, characters, and learning moments that empower all kids to become lifelong readers and learners through bestselling children’s books, literacy- and knowledge-building resources for schools including classroom magazines, and award-winning, entertaining children's media. As the world's largest publisher and distributor of children's books through school-based book clubs and book fairs, classroom libraries, school and public libraries, retail, and online, and with a global reach into more than 135 countries, Scholastic encourages the personal and intellectual growth of all children, while nurturing a lifelong relationship with reading, themselves, and the world around them. Learn more at www.scholastic.com.

Some benefits that we offer:

 

* Full suite of health and wellness benefits (including a $0 deductible Medical Plan)
* Retirement Savings Plan 401(k) with options for both Roth and Traditional Contributions
* Tuition-Free programs for undergraduate and graduate degrees
* Generous Parental Leave Program
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with opportunity for discounted stock at a 15% discount

Thank you for your consideration in choosing Scholastic.

card.title: GEUS/PLANT MANAGER
card.description:
**FUNCTION:**

Responsible for the management, operation, maintenance, and performance of GEUS electric generation facilities. Provides technical and administrative leadership to ensure safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective plant operations; maintains equipment reliability and ensures applicable compliance obligations are met; develops employees; and ensures adherence to established policies, procedures, and applicable requirements.

 

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Manage the operation, maintenance, and performance of GEUS electric generating facilities together with its associated transmission substations and their interconnections to support safe, reliable, and efficient electric generation.
* Oversee plant and equipment condition, identify deficiencies, coordinate preventative and corrective maintenance activities with the Maintenance Supervisor.
* Assist in development of departmental budget, implement approved budget, monitor expenses, analyze variances and recommend corrective actions.
* Provide leadership, supervision, and performance management for the Production Department, establishing clear expectations and promoting accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Oversee the preparation and accuracy of material requisitions, equipment reports, fuel consumption reports, and other operational records required for effective plant management.
* Oversee the development and implementation of work plans, shift schedules, and staffing assignments to ensure adequate coverage and continuity of plant operations.
* Ensure periodic inspections and assessments of generating equipment, transmission substations, radio communications systems, buildings, and associated facilities are performed and deficiencies are addressed.
* Oversee the monthly accounting and reporting of generated energy.
* Ensure compliance with applicable environmental and regulatory compliance requirements, operational and maintenance procedures, processes, and other organizational requirements.
* Maintain a safe, clean, and orderly working environment by reinforcing safe work practices, addressing identified hazards, and promoting a positive safety culture.
* Ensure appropriate physical security measures are maintained to protect plant facilities, equipment, personnel, and other critical assets. Participate in the development and evaluation of cost-benefit analyses, operational improvements, and capital projects to support informed decision-making and responsible use of utility resources. Identify and maintain an appropriate inventory of critical power production parts, evaluate inventory requirements, associated costs.
* Ensure plant operating and maintenance procedures are accurate, complete, current, and appropriate; oversee their development review and revisions as necessary.
* Participate in meetings to enhance compliance, safety, and communication with subordinates and superiors
* Communicate significant operational issues, equipment deficiencies, reliability concerns, regulatory matters, and material changes in work activities in a timely manner.
* Identify opportunities to improve plant reliability, operational efficiency, maintenance practices, and cost effectiveness; recommend and implement approved improvements.
* Perform other related duties as assigned.

 

*This general overview only includes essential functions of the job and does not imply that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee occupying this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other job-related duties requested by supervisor or management.*

 

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS:**

* Any combination of education, training, and experience equivalent to an Associate of Applied Science (A.A.S.) or Associate of Science (A.S.) degree in Engineering, Science or Technology or related field, and at least ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in electric power generating, including at least two (2) years in a supervisory or management capacity. Equivalent training or experience
* Comprehensive knowledge of electric power generation facilities, including steam turbines and reciprocating engine generation systems; associated machinery and equipment; operating and maintenance requirements., and related distribution/ transmission substations and electrical interconnections.
* Considerable knowledge of occupational hazards and applicable safety practices associated with electric power generation, industrial facilities, electrical equipment, and high-voltage systems.
* Knowledge of supervisory principles, employee development, performance management, and training methods, with the ability to plan, assign, coordinate, and evaluate the work of subordinate personnel.
* Working knowledge of applicable environmental laws, regulations, permits, safety requirements, and reporting procedures related to electric power generation, with the ability to ensure compliance with established requirements.
* Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, and maintain productive working relationships with utility officials, employees, contractors, regulatory representatives, and the public.
* Ability to evaluate plant operations and maintenance, analyze technical and financial information, identify deficiencies and opportunities for improvement, make sound decisions, and manage departmental resources, including budgets, to support reliability, efficiency, and cost control.

 

**PHYSICAL EFFORT:**

* Moderate physical requirements; must be capable of climbing stairs and ladders

card.title: Health Plan Quality Director
card.description:
Community Health Plan of Imperial Valley (CHPIV) is Imperial County's Medi-Cal managed care plan. We are a locally managed public health care plan committed to working with members, providers, and the residents of Imperial County.

As we continue to build something great, we are looking for a Quality Director to be responsible for the strategic development, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of CHPIV's Quality Improvement Program and Performance Improvement initiatives.

**Our next team member will do the following:**

* Direct and oversee CHPIV's Quality Improvement Program and related performance improvement activities.
* Collaborate with the Chief Medical Officer and Health Equity Officer to establish organizational quality and health equity goals, priorities, and strategies.
* Lead initiatives designed to improve clinical outcomes, member experience, preventive health measures, access to care, and care coordination.
* Develop, implement, and monitor quality improvement and health equity work plans.
* Monitor organizational performance measures and identify opportunities for improvement in quality, health outcomes, and equitable access to services.
* Partner with clinical and operational departments to reduce health disparities and improve outcomes among underserved and vulnerable populations.
* Support initiatives addressing social determinants of health, cultural and linguistic needs, and barriers to healthcare access.
* Coordinate quality studies, performance improvement projects, corrective action plans, and follow-up monitoring activities.
* Facilitate Quality Improvement Committee meetings and other quality-related workgroups.
* Develop executive summaries, committee reports, dashboards, presentations, and Board reports regarding quality and health equity performance.
* Support readiness activities and responses related to CMS, DHCS, DMHC, NCQA, and other regulatory requirements.
* Partner with delegated entities, providers, community organizations, and internal stakeholders to improve quality and member outcomes.
* Develop, review, and maintain quality management plans, policies, procedures, annual evaluations, and supporting documentation.
* Monitor project timelines, implementation activities, risks, and barriers to successful program execution.
* Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and performance management for assigned staff.
* Promote a culture of continuous quality improvement, accountability, innovation, and health equity.

**You may be right for this job if you have the following:**

* Five (5) years of experience in managed care, healthcare quality, utilization management, care management, population health, compliance, clinical operations, or related healthcare programs.
* Two (2) or more years of program, project, or operational leadership experience supporting quality, regulatory, performance improvement, or healthcare initiatives.
* Three (3) years of progressive leadership, management, or supervisory experience.
* Experience leading quality improvement, clinical operations, regulatory compliance, accreditation, or performance improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing cross-functional projects and organizational initiatives.
* Experience collaborating with physicians, healthcare providers, executive leadership, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Experience developing policies, procedures, reports, presentations, and organizational work plans.
* Experience working within a managed care or healthcare delivery environment.
* Experience analyzing quality, clinical, operational, or regulatory performance data and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
* Knowledge of healthcare quality programs, accreditation standards, and regulatory requirements, including CMS, DHCS, DMHC, and NCQA.
* Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures, corrective action plans, quality initiatives, and operational improvement strategies.
* Strong project management, analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with physicians, executive leadership, providers, health equity leaders, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate complex concepts to diverse audiences.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

**Our commitment to you:**

* A competitive salary of $130,000-$160,000/ year
* Health, dental and vision insurance for you and your family covered 85%
* Generous paid time off
* A retirement plan with a generous match
* A chance to make a real difference in the Imperial Valley community

Preference will be given to candidates who are local to Imperial, California, but remote candidates living in California will also be considered.

We are an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

card.title: Regional Director, Food Safety and Quality Assurance
card.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

*We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.*

**SUMMARY:** The Regional Food Safety and Quality Assurance Director is responsible for ensuring company compliance with appropriate food safety laws and regulations including but not limited to FSIS, HACCP, SSOP and GMP requirements. Additionally, this position is responsible for ensuring company compliance with appropriate customer expectations regarding specifications, quality, procedures, or any special requirement

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include, but are not limited to, the following:

* Demonstrate proficient knowledge of procedures currently written for monitoring processes on the production floor and ensure proper implementation and enforcement. This includes but is not limited to:
 + HACCP (Hazardous Analysis of Critical Control Points) integration into the facility
 + QA (Quality Assurance) procedures.
 + SSOP (Standard Sanitation Operating Procedures)
 + SOP (Standard Operating Procedures)
 + GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices)
 + Pre-Operation Inspection
 + Bone Elimination
 + Food Defense
* Provide day-to-day leadership for plant management regarding food safety regulations, procedures, and issues.
* Demonstrate a complete understanding of the HACCP, Food Defense and SSOP procedures as well as the regulatory process and supporting documents that are included.
* Possess a complete working knowledge of the Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) regulations, implementing directives and other appropriate food safety guidance material that affects our plant and products.
* Oversee the implementation of any new food safety and/or quality procedures affecting the plant.
* Maintain plant and departmental records, report and log to ensure documentation and design controls are appropriate, and that record retention requirements are met.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

This position will have supervisory responsibility.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* **Required**
 + Bachelor’s Degree in Food Science or related field or equivalent related experience AND 7+ years of experience in food processing, food safety & quality assurance OR 11+ years of progressively responsible FSQA related experience
 + Excellent interpersonal and communication skills – written and verbal
 + Proficient computer skills, especially in Microsoft applications (Excel, Power Point, Outlook etc.)
 + Working knowledge of Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) management system required by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the standards set by the Safe Quality Food Institute (SQFI)
* **Preferred**
 + Experience with Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS), Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) regulations
 + Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) Certification
 + ServSafe Basic Certification
 + Poultry experience

*George’s is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to, among others, individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans. If you need an accommodation because of a disability to search, apply or interview for a career opportunity with the Company, please send an email to compliance@georgesinc.com or call 479-927-7000 to let us know the nature of your request and your contact information to assist you*

*We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disabled/Veterans*

card.title: Sr Manager, Quality Planning & Strategy
card.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.
 
 
**Job Description**

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Global Quality Project & Portfolio Management

* Own and maintain Global Quality project portfolios, ensuring visibility, alignment, and execution across the network.
* Monitor project progress, proactively manage risks and dependencies, and ensure initiatives are delivered on time and within scope.
* Drive end‑to‑end planning and execution of global quality initiatives, including detailed project plans, timelines, milestones, and resource management.
Collaborate closely with Project Leads and Quality Leadership to track progress, manage risks, and communicate outcomes across the organization. 

 

Quality Systems Enablement & Integration

* Capture, prioritize, and manage Quality Systems enhancements and platform integrations, ensuring timely and effective implementation.
* Support the annual Quality Planning process, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives and enterprise priorities.
Develop, organize, and maintain comprehensive QA and QC project documentation, dashboards, and performance reporting. 

 

Governance, Communication & Reporting

* Facilitate regular project updates, steering committee meetings, quality forums, and executive‑level reporting.
* Measure Quality project performance using appropriate systems, tools, and methodologies, including defining and tracking KPIs related to project success, quality impact, and operational outcomes.
Leverage data‑driven insights to inform decision‑making and drive continuous improvement. 

 

Continuous Improvement & Change Enablement

* Perform and assess project and quality risk management, escalating critical risks and mitigation strategies to leadership as needed.
* Identify and implement opportunities for process efficiency, automation, and innovation across Quality initiatives.
Apply Organizational Change Management (OCM) strategies, as appropriate, to support adoption, sustainability, and business readiness. 

 

Stakeholder & Team Leadership

* Manage stakeholder relationships across all phases of the project lifecycle, engaging effectively with global, cross‑functional partners.
* Guide and mentor junior Quality staff, fostering a culture of quality excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Stay current on industry trends, regulatory changes, and best practices to proactively enhance Quality systems and processes. 

 

Knowledge & Skills

* Strong knowledge of Quality Systems, Quality principles, industry standards, and best practices.
* Excellent problem‑solving, analytical, and attention‑to‑detail skills.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior and executive audiences.
* Demonstrated strength in planning, prioritization, and managing multiple initiatives simultaneously.
* Familiarity with project management tools, stakeholder management practices, and performance tracking methodologies.
* Proven ability to engage and influence internal and external stakeholders, facilitate discussions, delegate effectively, and drive accountability.
* Self‑motivated, proactive, highly organized, and results‑oriented with a strong sense of urgency.
* Ability to navigate ambiguity and translate complex initiatives into clear, actionable execution plans.
* Comfortable balancing competing priorities in a fast‑paced environment while fostering a collaborative, trust‑based culture.
PMP and/or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification is a plus. 

 

Basic Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in a science‑related field (e.g., Life Sciences, Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, or related discipline).
* At least 8 years of relevant industry experience in Quality, Quality Systems, Project Management, or regulated environments

OR

Master’s degree in a related field with at least 6 years of relevant industry experience. 

 

Preferred Qualifications

* Advanced degree in a science, engineering, or quality‑related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience managing global Quality projects or portfolios in regulated pharmaceutical, biotech, or medical device environments.
* Experience supporting Quality Systems, QA/QC initiatives, and cross‑functional quality transformations.
* Familiarity with project governance, executive reporting, and KPI‑driven performance management.
Project Management Professional (PMP) and/or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification
